risk_if_not_implemented: Without Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) Disposition, organizational data and assets may be retained, reused or improperly destroyed by the outgoing provider after the relationship ends. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Retention / Inability to Dispose of Data (R-AM-3), Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Supplier Financial Distress / Insolvency (MT-24).

compensating_control_1.name: Digital & Non-Digital Media Disposal
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to securely dispose of, destroy and/or erase digital and non-digital media when it is no longer required, using organization-defined procedures.
compensating_control_1.justification: Digital & Non-Digital Media Disposal (DCH-17) compensates for the absence of Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) Disposition (TPM-24.3) by defining the organization's standard for secure disposal, destruction and erasure of media, which sets the requirement the third party is expected to meet at cessation. Given the data-handling nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Third-Party Contract Requirements
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to require contractual requirements for applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements with third-parties, reflecting the organization's needs to protect its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).
compensating_control_2.justification: Third-Party Contract Requirements (TPM-14) compensates for the absence of Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) Disposition (TPM-24.3) by specifying return, retention and destruction obligations in third-party contracts, which is the only mechanism that binds the provider's handling of organizational Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) after service ends. Given the data-handling nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
